question_text: A municipal health office received a budget increase from ₱800,000 to ₱1,000,000. What was the percentage increase in its budget?

hint_ladder.title: Hanapin ang actual na dagdag
hint_ladder.text: Compute the difference: new minus old. Dito, ₱1,000,000 - ₱800,000 = ₱200,000. Yun ang basehan ng percent.

hint_ladder.title: Original ang base, hindi ang bago
hint_ladder.text: Sa percent increase, lagi mong gamiting base ay yung original na halaga, hindi yung bago. Mali ang mag-base sa 1M.

hint_ladder.title: Gawing fraction ang dagdag sa original
hint_ladder.text: I-divide ang 200,000 sa 800,000. Simpleng fraction: 1/4. Pag isipin mo, ilang beses pumapasok ang 200k sa 800k?

hint_ladder.title: I-convert ang fraction sa percent
hint_ladder.text: Multiply ang fraction sa 100. 1/4 × 100 = 25%. Kaya ang sagot ay 25%. Tandaan: 'Dagdag ÷ Original × 100'.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you divided the increase by the new budget (200k/1M=20%) instead of the original 800k. Always use the sta...

B.text: Correct. The increase is ₱200,000, original is ₱800,000, so fraction is 1/4 or 25%.

C.text: You might have chosen C because you miscalculated the fraction; 200k/800k simplifies to 1/4, not 3/10. Double-check your division.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you divided old by new (800k/1M=80%), which gives the ratio, not the percentage increase.

next_time_rule: For percentage increase, always use the formula: (Change / Original) x 100. The original number is your anchor.
